claims.title: Society of the liurai
claims.summary: Timor is organized into numerous small kingdoms ruled by hereditary chiefs, the liurai, whose authority rests on kinship, ritual, and the sacred houses central to Timorese culture.

sources.label: Indonesia: A Country Study (Federal Research Division)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1000bce-society-of-the-liurai, claim TL:TLS:event:1000bce:society-of-the-liurai, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The sandalwood trade
claims.summary: Timor's prized aromatic sandalwood is traded across maritime Asia to China, India, and beyond, drawing Malay, Chinese, and other merchants and giving the island wide renown.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-500bce-the-sandalwood-trade, claim TL:TLS:event:500bce:the-sandalwood-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portuguese arrival and missions
claims.summary: Portuguese traders seeking sandalwood and Dominican missionaries reach Timor and the Solor archipelago, beginning Catholic conversion and a loose Portuguese presence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1515-portuguese-arrival-and-missions, claim TL:TLS:event:1515:portuguese-arrival-and-missions, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capital established at Dili
claims.summary: The Portuguese move their administrative seat from Lifau in Oecusse to Dili on the north coast, which becomes the lasting capital of Portuguese Timor.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1769-capital-established-at-dili, claim TL:TLS:event:1769:capital-established-at-dili, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Partition of the island
claims.summary: A Portuguese-Dutch treaty divides Timor between Dutch West Timor and Portuguese East Timor, leaving Portugal the eastern half plus the Oecusse enclave; the border is finalized in the early 20th century.

sources.label: Boundaries in the Island of Timor (Netherlands v. Portugal), Award of 25 June 1914

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1859-partition-of-the-island, claim TL:TLS:event:1859:partition-of-the-island, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Decolonization begins
claims.summary: After Portugal's Carnation Revolution, Lisbon moves to decolonize Timor; rival Timorese parties, the pro-independence Fretilin and pro-integration Apodeti, vie over the colony's future.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1974-decolonization-begins, claim TL:TLS:event:1974:decolonization-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Declaration of independence
claims.summary: Fretilin unilaterally proclaims the independent Democratic Republic of East Timor in Dili as Portugal withdraws and an Indonesian invasion looms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1975-declaration-of-independence, claim TL:TLS:event:1975:declaration-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Indonesian invasion
claims.summary: Indonesia launches a full-scale air and sea invasion of Dili, beginning an occupation marked from the start by mass civilian killing.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Timor-Leste
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1975-indonesian-invasion, claim TL:TLS:event:1975:indonesian-invasion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Annexation as 27th province
claims.summary: Indonesia formally annexes the territory as its 27th province, Timor Timur; the United Nations refuses to recognize the annexation and affirms Timorese self-determination.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1976-annexation-as-27th-province, claim TL:TLS:event:1976:annexation-as-27th-province, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Santa Cruz massacre
claims.summary: Indonesian troops fire on a peaceful pro-independence procession at Dili's Santa Cruz cemetery, killing at least 250; smuggled video footage brings the occupation to global attention.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1991-santa-cruz-massacre, claim TL:TLS:event:1991:santa-cruz-massacre, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capture of Xanana Gusmao
claims.summary: Indonesian forces capture resistance commander Xanana Gusmao in Dili; tried and sentenced to a long prison term in Jakarta, he continues to lead the movement from prison.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1992-capture-of-xanana-gusmao, claim TL:TLS:event:1992:capture-of-xanana-gusmao, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Nobel Peace Prize
claims.summary: Bishop Carlos Belo and Jose Ramos-Horta share the Nobel Peace Prize for their work toward a just and peaceful solution to the conflict in East Timor.

sources.label: The Nobel Peace Prize 1996: Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo and Jose Ramos-Horta
Secretary-General welcomes award of 1996 Nobel Peace Prize to Bishop Belo and Jose Ramos-Horta

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1996-nobel-peace-prize, claim TL:TLS:event:1996:nobel-peace-prize, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence referendum
claims.summary: In a UN-supervised popular consultation, 78.5 per cent of Timorese reject autonomy within Indonesia and choose a transition to independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1999-independence-referendum, claim TL:TLS:event:1999:independence-referendum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Post-ballot violence and INTERFET
claims.summary: Pro-Indonesian militias unleash killings and destruction, displacing some 500,000 people; the Australian-led INTERFET deploys from 20 September to restore order.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1999-post-ballot-violence-and-interfet, claim TL:TLS:event:1999:post-ballot-violence-and-interfet, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: UN administration established
claims.summary: Security Council Resolution 1272 creates UNTAET, granting the United Nations full authority to govern East Timor through the transition to independence.

sources.label: UNTAET (United Nations Transitional Administration in East Timor)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-1999-un-administration-established, claim TL:TLS:event:1999:un-administration-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Restoration of independence
claims.summary: UNTAET hands over sovereignty; Timor-Leste restores its independence with Xanana Gusmao as first president and soon joins the United Nations.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Timor-Leste
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: The 2006 crisis
claims.summary: The dismissal of disaffected soldiers triggers fighting in Dili that kills dozens and displaces tens of thousands, topples the prime minister, and brings back international peacekeepers.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-2006-the-2006-crisis, claim TL:TLS:event:2006:the-2006-crisis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Attack on the president
claims.summary: Rebel soldiers shoot and gravely wound President Jose Ramos-Horta and attack Prime Minister Xanana Gusmao's convoy; both survive and the rebellion collapses.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-2008-attack-on-the-president, claim TL:TLS:event:2008:attack-on-the-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Maritime boundary treaty with Australia
claims.summary: Timor-Leste and Australia sign a treaty settling their disputed Timor Sea boundary, the first reached through UN conciliation, resolving claims over the Greater Sunrise gas field.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Timor-Leste: From the sandalwood kingdoms of the liurai through four centuries of Portuguese rule and a brutal occupation to Asia's youngest nation.", terralore.co/country/TLS/chronicle#ev-2018-maritime-boundary-treaty-with-australia, claim TL:TLS:event:2018:maritime-boundary-treaty-with-australia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: ASEAN membership
claims.summary: Timor-Leste is admitted as the 11th member of ASEAN at the bloc's summit in Kuala Lumpur, its first enlargement in over two decades and the culmination of a years-long bid.

sources.label: History Is Made: Timor-Leste Becomes ASEAN's 11th Member
